pointers.sentence: A new instance given no value holds a `DatabaseDefault` in its place, unless the field has Django's default too (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field._get_default`; [The field classes](../models/field-types.md)).
`GeneratedField` (5.0) is a column the database computes from its row, and no save writes it (`django/db/models/fields/generated.py:GeneratedField`).
Since 5.2 a constraint over one can be validated (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._get_field_expression_map`).

Since 6.1 PostgreSQL from 18 may have a virtual one and Oracle from 23.7 a stored one; each had had only the other kind (`django/db/backends/postgresql/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.supports_virtual_generated_columns`, `django/db/backends/oracle/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.supports_stored_generated_columns`).

Since 6.1 PostgreSQL from 18 may have a virtual one and Oracle from 23.7 a stored one; each had had only the other kind (`django/db/backends/postgresql/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.supports_virtual_generated_columns`, `django/db/backends/oracle/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.supports_stored_generated_columns`).
Since 6.0 `Model._save_table` reads back a field assigned an expression, and after an update the generated fields that depend on a field it writes (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._save_table`).

On MySQL, and on MariaDB after an update, the backend cannot return the columns, so the field is ordinarily deferred to the next read (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._assign_returned_values`; [Saving an instance](../instance/saving.md#what-comes-back)).

Since 6.0 a save's insert, unless raw, calls `django.db.models.Field.pre_save` twice for each field it writes, where 5.2.17 called it once (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._save_table`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLInsertCompiler.pre_save_val`; [Saving an instance](../instance/saving.md#pre_save-and-why-an-insert-calls-it-twice)).

Since 6.0 a save's insert, unless raw, calls `django.db.models.Field.pre_save` twice for each field it writes, where 5.2.17 called it once (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._save_table`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLInsertCompiler.pre_save_val`; [Saving an instance](../instance/saving.md#pre_save-and-why-an-insert-calls-it-twice)).
Since 6.1 the three `DatabaseOnDelete` values of `on_delete` leave the related rows to the `ON DELETE` clause the schema editor writes (`django/db/models/deletion.py:DatabaseOnDelete`).
They are in `SKIP_COLLECTION` with `DO_NOTHING`, so a delete's `Collector` passes the relation over (`django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.collect`).

It fetches them first where a receiver of `pre_delete` or `post_delete` must be called for them, or their own relations followed (`django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.can_fast_delete`, `django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.sort`).

It fetches them first where a receiver of `pre_delete` or `post_delete` must be called for them, or their own relations followed (`django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.can_fast_delete`, `django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.sort`).
The 6.1 notes give the saved fetch as the reason, and the unsent signals as its consequence (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`; [Deleting: the `Collector`](../instance/deleting.md)).
The checks refuse a chain of keys that mixes the database's actions with the collector's (`django/db/models/fields/related.py:ForeignKey._check_on_delete`).
`Collector.delete` sends `post_delete` only for the rows it collected, and counts only what it deletes (`django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.delete`).
`CompositePrimaryKey` (5.2) is a field without a column, assigned to `pk`, whose value is a tuple (`django/db/models/fields/composite.py:CompositePrimaryKey`).

Since 6.0 the check `"models.E049"` refuses a `ForeignObject` of several `from_fields=` named in an index, a constraint or `Options.unique_together`; 5.2.17 let one pass (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._check_local_fields`).
`Model._is_pk_set` counts a key unset when it is `None` or a tuple with a part unset, and since 6.1 when it holds a `DatabaseDefault` (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._is_pk_set`).

Since 6.2 `Model.__eq__` asks it, and an unsaved instance whose key is unset is equal only to itself; before, it compared any key but `None` (`django/db/models/base.py:Model.__eq__`; [An instance and its state](../instance/state.md)).
Two with the same whole key still are, though the 6.2 notes say unsaved instances with a composite key "no longer compare equal to other instances" (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).
The automatic key's default became `BigAutoField` in 6.0, and the warning models.W042 went with it (`django/conf/global_settings.py`; [What changed](../changes.md#an-old-habit-release-by-release)).

The setter of `Field.choices` passes them to `normalize_choices`, which makes the pairs (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.choices`, `django/utils/choices.py:normalize_choices`; [Choices: `normalize_choices` and the choice iterators](../utils/choices.md)).

The setter of `Field.choices` passes them to `normalize_choices`, which makes the pairs (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.choices`, `django/utils/choices.py:normalize_choices`; [Choices: `normalize_choices` and the choice iterators](../utils/choices.md)).
`USE_BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` brings the dashes back until Django 2028 (`django/db/models/utils.py:get_blank_choice_label`; [What changed in forms and validators](forms.md)).
Since 6.0 a `CheckConstraint` given `check=` raises a `TypeError`: 5.1 had deprecated it for `condition=` (`django/db/models/constraints.py:CheckConstraint.__init__`).

Since 6.0 the method `BaseConstraint.check` gives `Model._check_constraints` the system check's messages; under 5.2.17 `check` was a `CheckConstraint`'s condition, with a warning (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._check_constraints`).
Since 5.2 it uses a message given, with the code given (`django/db/models/constraints.py:UniqueConstraint.validate`).
The 5.2 notes say the code and the message "are now always used when provided" (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`).
